taskDescription: Complete the crossword using key terms from MI10.1-5 | Healthcare-Associated Infections.

words.clue: This multi-drug resistant bacterium is a major causative agent of surgical site infections and catheter-related bloodstream infections.
This fungal organism commonly causes catheter-associated urinary tract infections in hospitalized patients.
This gram-negative bacterium is the primary causative agent of ventilator-associated pneumonia in ICU patients.
The most common mode of HAI transmission occurs through direct or indirect patient and healthcare worker interaction.
Infections like influenza and meningococcal disease require this precaution type for particles larger than 5 micrometers.
This precaution type is needed for infections transmitted by tiny droplet nuclei that remain suspended in air.
Prolonged use of this medical device in the urinary or vascular system significantly increases HAI risk.
Use of this mechanical breathing device for more than 48 hours increases the risk of hospital-acquired pneumonia.
This personal protective equipment must be worn whenever there is contact with patient blood or body fluids.
This carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacterium is an emerging nosocomial pathogen with high mortality in ICU settings.
The source of infectious agents in HAI transmission chains includes colonized patients and contaminated environmental surfaces.
